facts.statement: Fossils of Gobititan were discovered in the Gongpoquan Basin in Gansu, China, during the summer of 1999.
facts.quote: Its remains were recovered in the summer of 1999 at the "Middle Gray unit" (also known as the Xiagou Formation) of the Xinminbao Group in the Gongpoquan Basin in Gansu, China.

facts.statement: The type specimen is a partial skeleton containing 41 tail vertebrae and an incomplete left hindlimb.
facts.quote: The genus is based on one partial skeleton, holotype IVPP 12579, which consists of a series of 41 caudal vertebrae and an incomplete left hindlimb.

facts.statement: The species Gobititan shenzhouensis was named and described by You, Tang, and Luo in 2003.
facts.quote: The type species, Gobititan shenzhouensis was named and described by You, Tang and Luo in 2003

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Gobi Desert region and Greek Titans to reflect the animal's large size.
facts.quote: The name of this genus is derived from the Gobi Desert region and the Titans of Greek mythology, which is a reference to its large body size.

facts.statement: The specific name shenzhouensis refers to Shenzhou, an ancient name for China.
facts.quote: The specific name shenzhouensis, is derived from "Shenzhou", an ancient name for China.

facts.statement: Gobititan possessed a relatively high number of tail vertebrae compared to advanced titanosaurs, a trait interpreted as basal.
facts.quote: Compared with advanced titanosaurs, where the number of caudal vertebrae had been reduced to less than 35, Gobititan had a relatively high number of caudal vertebrae, which was interpreted as a basal trait.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated that Gobititan reached a length of 20 meters and a weight of 20 metric tons.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated that Gobititan was 20 m long and weighed 20 MT.

facts.statement: Gobititan was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur living during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Gobititan is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur from the Aptian faunal stage of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Recent research generally classifies Gobititan as a titanosauriform and a member of the Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: more recent research has generally considered it to be a titanosauriform, more specifically a member of the Somphospondyli.

facts.statement: Gobititan is distinguished by the presence of a fifth digit on its foot, a trait unknown in other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: based on the fact that the fifth digit is still present on the foot (a trait unknown in all other titanosaurs)

facts.statement: Some scientific analyses still classify Gobititan as a titanosaur despite recent trends placing it in Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, some analyses still recover Gobititan as a titanosaur.

facts.statement: Gobititan lived during the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Gobititan as Euhelopodidae.
